englishSourceNotes: 'My favorite bug': the row includes snail, spider and worm, which are not bugs/insects; 'critter' or 'little creature' would be accurate (nl uses 'beestje', which covers all).
'My favorite clothes' is plural but the child circles ONE item; 'My favorite thing to wear' fits better.
'My favorite treat' row includes pancake and muffin, which also appear under breakfast (overlap between copies 3 and 5).
'I can catch a fish' states an outcome, not a skill (and the cue is a fishing rod); 'I can go fishing' is the skill.
'I can play a board game' is cued by a single die, not a board; acceptable but loose.
'I can swing high' adds a boast; 'I can swing by myself' is the real K milestone.
'I can walk a long way' is fine, but the hiking cue suggests 'I can go for a long walk'.
'I can play the guitar' is rare at age 5; most children will leave it unticked (fine for a checklist, but consider 'I can play an instrument').

optionWordFlags.problem: picture is a plain untoasted slice of bread; a Dutch child calls it 'boterham' (or 'brood'); 'toast' in nl means crispbread/rusk-like toast

noun among verb labels (fietsen, zwemmen, schilderen); 'voetballen' would be consistent. Same for 'basketbal' (basketballen) and 'tennis' (tennissen) — acceptable as nouns but the row is mixed

otherNotes: Heading lengths: 'Mijn lievelingshuisdier' and 'Mijn lievelingsvoertuig' are 23 chars; 'Mijn lievelingsinstrument' is 25 and is one unbreakable 20-letter word on line 2 — check it fits the narrow box. If not, use 'Mijn liefste instrument' (23).

farm: 'Mijn lievelingsboerderijdier' (28, one 23-letter word) cannot wrap in a narrow box, so I used 'Mijn lievelingsdier op de boerderij', which breaks cleanly into two lines ('Mijn lievelingsdier' / 'op de boerderij'). It reuses the shipped animal heading as its first line, which reads naturally.
treat: 'lekkers' covers cake, pancake and sweets; 'snoep' would be wrong for cake/pancake/waffle.
dress: 'me zelf aankleden' (by myself) is the natural kleuter phrasing; 'mezelf aankleden' is also correct but stiffer.
kite: 'vliegeren' is the everyday Dutch verb, shorter and more natural than 'een vlieger oplaten'.
drum: uses 'trommel' to match the option word printed in the instrument row.
All 'can' sentences follow the shipped 'Ik kan …' pattern, max 30 characters, no digits.
